About Me

About Me

I’m MD Shahid Hussain, an IT professional, corporate trainer, and entrepreneur with over 15 years of experience across technology services, enterprise systems, and professional learning. I hold a Master of Computer Applications (MCA) from Pune University.

My career has been shaped by a simple belief: technology creates value when people can rely on it, understand it, and use it to improve their work. That belief has guided me through technical support, Oracle database and applications administration, corporate training, resource coordination, and business leadership.

A Career Across Technology and Learning

My technical background includes Oracle Apps DBA, Oracle database administration, and IT support. These roles have taught me to investigate problems carefully, support important business systems, and explain technical matters in ways that help people make informed decisions.

Corporate training has also been a significant part of my journey. I have worked to connect organisations with technology trainers and learning resources, support training engagements, and make complex subjects easier for professionals to understand and apply. This combination of IT and training experience helps me see both how a system works and what people need to use it confidently.

Leadership and Entrepreneurship

I previously served as Director and CEO of ANT GLOBAL SOFT PRIVATE LIMITED and AMOLI JEWELLERS PRIVATE LIMITED. These roles gave me firsthand experience in building businesses, coordinating teams, managing relationships, and making decisions under real operating constraints.

At ANT GLOBAL SOFT, my work was connected to corporate IT training and technology services. My leadership role at AMOLI JEWELLERS broadened my understanding of business operations and customer needs.

These are former roles. I am no longer involved in either company, and both companies have put their services on hold. The experience of leading them continues to shape how I approach challenges and opportunities.

My Focus Today

I am expanding my expertise in AI Product Management, product and design thinking, Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG), prompt engineering, and AI automation. I am especially interested in practical AI use cases that help organisations improve workflows, find information, and support better decisions.

I hope to bring my background in enterprise technology, training, and business operations into product work. My approach begins with understanding the people affected by a problem, then shaping a solution that is useful, responsible, and grounded in real needs.

A Purpose Beyond Business

During the COVID-19 period, I helped organise ration distribution in villages, reaching more than 500 people. That experience reinforced something I believe deeply: meaningful work should improve lives, especially for people who have limited access to support.

My long-term aim is to build a school and a hospital that serve families with limited financial means. I want children to have access to quality education and families to receive dependable medical care, either free of cost or at a price they can afford. This vision includes people living in poverty as well as middle-class families who may struggle with the rising cost of education and healthcare.

I know this is an ambitious goal that will take time, resources, and the right partners. It is a goal I want to work toward throughout my life, because a person’s financial circumstances should not determine the quality of education or medical care they can receive.

What Drives Me

My professional experience brings together technical operations, corporate learning, entrepreneurship, and emerging AI products. My personal ambition gives that work a wider purpose. I want to keep learning, build useful solutions, and create opportunities that make a lasting difference for people and communities.

Digital Marketing & Media Services

Digital marketing works best when every activity serves a clear purpose. A business needs to know whom it wants to reach, what it wants to communicate, and what action it hopes people will take. My interest in digital marketing is rooted in that connection between business goals, useful content, and measurable results.

Drawing on my experience in IT, corporate training, and business coordination, I am particularly interested in digital marketing for technology companies, training providers, educational institutions, and professional services organisations. The following are planned service areas.

1. Digital Marketing Strategy

A practical marketing plan begins with an understanding of the organisation, its audience, and its goals. This area would cover audience research, positioning, channel selection, campaign objectives, content themes, and a publishing plan. The aim would be to give each activity a defined role, whether it supports awareness, enquiries, event registrations, or stronger relationships with existing audiences.

2. Social Media Management

A professional social presence should communicate consistently and give people a reason to follow or engage. This area would include profile reviews, content calendars, post coordination, community engagement, and performance reviews for relevant platforms such as LinkedIn, Facebook, and Instagram. The choice of platform and content would depend on the organisation’s audience and objectives.

3. Content Creation and Brand Communication

Clear content helps an organisation explain what it does and why it matters. Planned content formats include social posts, service descriptions, educational articles, campaign messages, event announcements, brochures, and short video scripts. My focus would be on making technical or specialised offerings understandable while preserving their professional credibility.

4. Brand Identity and Digital Presence

People should be able to recognise an organisation and understand its message wherever they encounter it. This area would cover the coordination of page descriptions, visual direction, tone of voice, key messages, and campaign materials. The goal would be a consistent presentation across social profiles, websites, and promotional content.

5. Search Visibility and Website Content

A website should be easy to find, easy to understand, and easy to use. This planned area would include reviewing page titles and descriptions, organising service pages, improving the clarity of website copy, and identifying technical or content issues that affect search visibility. Search performance and indexing information would help guide priorities.

6. Paid Social Campaigns

Paid campaigns can help an organisation reach a defined audience when there is a clear offer and a way to assess results. This area would involve campaign planning, audience and message development, creative coordination, landing page alignment, and performance review. Potential uses include promoting training programmes, events, services, and enquiry forms.

7. Lead Generation and Follow-Up

An enquiry is useful only when it reaches the right team and receives an appropriate response. This planned service would connect campaign messages with enquiry forms, landing pages, lead tracking, and follow-up workflows. For training providers, this could support demo registrations, course enquiries, corporate training requests, or partnership discussions.

8. Email Campaigns and Audience Nurturing

Email can help an organisation continue a useful conversation with people who have chosen to hear from it. This area would include audience grouping, newsletter planning, event invitations, follow-up messages, and campaign reporting. The emphasis would be on sending relevant information to the right audience at the right stage of their relationship with the organisation.

9. Reporting and Improvement

Digital activity should be reviewed against its original goal. Reporting would bring together relevant measures such as reach, engagement, website visits, enquiries, registrations, and campaign costs. The purpose would be to understand what is working, identify where people lose interest, and make informed improvements over time.

Work & Impact

Projects & Use Cases

Six prioritised Oracle EBS use case ideas, followed by portfolio work in Oracle operations, AI product thinking, and RAG-assisted learning. The six ideas are proposed concepts; no client deployment or measured result is claimed here.

Priority 1 · Oracle EBS · Proposed AI Use Case
EBS Incident Copilot
Need
Support teams need faster access to relevant runbooks, known errors, and incident history when diagnosing EBS issues.
Concept
Retrieve approved support knowledge and suggest likely checks, related incidents, and next steps with source references for DBA review.
Safeguard
An authorised engineer verifies evidence and approves any production action.
Oracle EBSRAGIncident Triage
Priority 2 · Oracle EBS · Proposed Analytics Use Case
Concurrent Request Failure Predictor
Need
Repeated or high-risk concurrent request failures can interrupt business processing.
Concept
Analyse request history, error patterns, scheduling, and runtime signals to flag requests that may need attention before the next run.
Safeguard
Validate predictions against historical data and keep alert thresholds under operations-team control.
Concurrent ManagerPredictive Analytics
Priority 3 · Oracle EBS · Proposed Operations Use Case
Patching Readiness Assistant
Need
Patching preparation requires consistent checks across dependencies, backups, approvals, and change windows.
Concept
Build an evidence-based readiness checklist for EBS patching, highlighting missing prerequisites and linking each check to the approved procedure.
Safeguard
DBA and change teams retain final approval; the assistant does not apply patches.
EBS PatchingChange Readiness
Priority 4 · Oracle Database · Proposed Dashboard
Database Health & Capacity Dashboard
Need
DBAs need a clear view of health signals and capacity trends across environments.
Concept
Combine approved monitoring data for storage growth, availability, backup status, and workload trends in one reviewable dashboard.
Safeguard
Show collection time, thresholds, and data source so teams can investigate alerts in context.
Oracle DatabaseMonitoring
Priority 5 · Oracle EBS · Proposed Governance Use Case
EBS Access Review Assistant
Need
Periodic reviews of user responsibilities and access can be difficult to coordinate and document.
Concept
Prepare reviewer-friendly summaries of assigned access, exceptions, and approval history for the authorised access owner.
Safeguard
Apply least-privilege data handling; only authorised owners decide access changes.
Access ReviewGovernance
Priority 6 · Oracle EBS · Proposed Operations Use Case
Clone & Environment Readiness Tracker
Need
A refreshed EBS environment needs many checks before it is safe to hand over for testing.
Concept
Track clone prerequisites, configuration steps, data protection, smoke tests, owners, and sign-off in a shared status view.
Safeguard
Require evidence and human sign-off for each critical readiness gate.
CloningReadiness

Insights & Learning

Blog

Reflections on enterprise technology, learning, and practical AI product thinking.

By MD Shahid Hussain · Career & Learning

From Oracle Apps DBA to AI Product Management: My Learning Journey

My career began with a practical question: how can technology help people do important work reliably? Over more than 15 years in IT, that question has taken me through technical support, Oracle database and applications administration, corporate training, resource coordination, and business leadership.

What Oracle systems taught me

Working around Oracle applications and databases taught me to look beyond an error message. A production issue can affect teams, timelines, and decisions. Good technical work starts with understanding the environment, investigating carefully, communicating clearly, and agreeing on the next step. Those habits remain valuable when exploring new technology.

Why people matter as much as systems

Training and resource coordination helped me see a different side of technology. A solution has little value if people cannot understand it or use it confidently. Listening to learners and organisations, defining the actual requirement, and connecting them with the right expertise made me more interested in the problems behind a request.

My move toward AI product thinking

Today I am building my knowledge in AI Product Management, product and design thinking, Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG), prompt engineering, and AI automation. I am interested in practical use cases: helping a support team find the right knowledge, making operational information easier to understand, or improving a workflow without adding unnecessary complexity.

For me, product thinking begins with a user and a problem. Who needs help? What do they do today? Where does the process fail? How would we know a proposed solution made their work better? AI can be part of the answer, but it needs clear goals, dependable information, human review where appropriate, and a way to measure results.

The journey ahead

I am still learning and applying these ideas. My background in enterprise systems, training, and leadership gives me useful context, while AI product work challenges me to keep asking better questions. I plan to share my learning, use cases, and practical observations here as that journey continues.

Oracle Apps DBA se AI Product Management tak: Mera Learning Journey

Mere career ki shuruaat ek practical sawaal se hui: technology logon ko unka zaroori kaam bharose ke saath karne mein kaise madad kar sakti hai? IT mein 15 saal se zyada ke safar mein maine technical support, Oracle database aur applications administration, corporate training, resource coordination aur business leadership par kaam kiya hai.

Oracle systems se kya seekha

Oracle applications aur databases ke saath kaam karte hue maine seekha ki sirf error message dekhna kaafi nahi hota. Production issue ka asar teams, timelines aur decisions par pad sakta hai. Pehle environment samajhna, issue ko dhyan se investigate karna, saaf communication rakhna aur phir next step tay karna zaroori hota hai. Ye aadatein nayi technology ke saath bhi kaam aati hain.

Systems ke saath log bhi zaroori hain

Training aur resource coordination ne mujhe technology ka doosra pehlu dikhaya. Agar log kisi solution ko samajh ya confidently use nahi kar paate, to uska fayda kam ho jata hai. Learners aur organisations ki baat sunna, actual requirement samajhna aur sahi expertise se jodna—isse meri dilchaspi request ke peeche ki problem mein badhi.

AI product thinking ki taraf mera safar

Aaj main AI Product Management, product aur design thinking, Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG), prompt engineering aur AI automation mein apni knowledge badha raha hoon. Mujhe practical use cases mein dilchaspi hai: support team ko sahi knowledge jaldi milna, operational information ko asaan banana, ya bina extra complexity ke workflow improve karna.

Mere liye product thinking user aur uski problem se shuru hoti hai. Madad kise chahiye? Aaj woh kaam kaise karta hai? Process kahan rukta hai? Kaise pata chalega ki solution se kaam behtar hua? AI ek hissa ho sakta hai, lekin clear goals, reliable information, zaroorat ke mutabiq human review aur results ko measure karna bhi zaroori hai.

Aage ka raasta

Main in ideas ko abhi seekh aur apply kar raha hoon. Enterprise systems, training aur leadership ka mera background mujhe context deta hai; AI product work mujhe behtar sawaal poochne ki challenge deta hai. Aage apni learning, use cases aur practical observations yahan share karunga.
